subject: Amber20 serial make test FAILUREs on IBM Power9

messages.author: Cong Liu
messages.body:
Dear Amber developer,
The Amber20 compiled with gcc/7.4.0 using the following command:
> *./configure --with-python MYPYTHON -nosse gnu*
failed some tests.
- Most of them are related to mdgx. I guess these are normal since using
the "-nosse" flag?
- Other nontrivial cpptraj test failures worry me.
I uploaded the diff and log files here:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14nRCTqOUAQ8DILypzE_lXCK2cLY_aY9B?usp=sharing
Thanks for looking into it!
Cong Liu

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Thu, May 21, 2020, Cong Liu wrote:
>
>The Amber20 compiled with gcc/7.4.0 using the following command:
>
>> *./configure --with-python MYPYTHON -nosse gnu*
>
>failed some tests.
>
> - Most of them are related to mdgx. I guess these are normal since using
> the "-nosse" flag?
> - Other nontrivial cpptraj test failures worry me.
Can you say more about your hardware and OS? I'm guessing that no
developer has tried to run these codes on Power9 chips; if I'm wrong,
presumably someone on the list will chime in. (I know that there are
people looking at putting Amber on Summit, but I've not heard either
news about this, or reports of problems.)
In a way, it is encouraging that the only problems are in mdgx, and in
some aspects of cpptraj. Dave Cerutti and Dan Roe may have more insight
here.
....dac

messages.author: Cong Liu
messages.body:
Hi Prof. Case,
Thanks for replying!
Can you say more about your hardware and OS?
The hardware is IBM POWER9 and V100. Here is the info provided by lscpu:
Architecture: ppc64le
Byte Order: Little Endian
CPU(s): 128
On-line CPU(s) list: 0-127
Thread(s) per core: 4
Core(s) per socket: 16
Socket(s): 2
NUMA node(s): 6
Model: 2.1 (pvr 004e 1201)
Model name: POWER9, altivec supported
The operating system is *Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) version 7.6.
*And it is
the Summit supercomputer.
Best,
Cong
